title: J-CRe3: A Japanese Conversation Dataset for Real-world Reference Resolution
abstract: Provides conversational data in which linguistic referring expressions are linked across modalities to real-world objects represented by bounding boxes. It covers direct and indirect references and supplies empirical transfer evidence for language-to-region grounding.

title: Ferret-UI: Grounded Mobile UI Understanding with Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Extends region-level multimodal understanding to mobile UI screenshots with tasks including referring, grounding, and reasoning over interface regions. Its region annotations and empirical benchmarks provide transfer evidence for expression-to-region grounding on structured screenshots.

title: Detecting Changes in XML Documents
abstract: Presents an XML differencing method that uses persistent node identifiers to track document components across versions and represents insertions, deletions, updates, and subtree moves. The method is empirically evaluated on synthetic data and web-derived XML documents and provides direct structured-document evidence for persistent element identity.

title: Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering using Self-Attention Scoring Mechanism
abstract: Addresses multi-page DocVQA by assigning relevance scores to pages and selecting pertinent pages before answer generation. Experiments study document collections containing many pages, providing empirical page-level evidence localization but not exact region or cell provenance.
venue: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2024)

title: GRAVL-BERT: Graphical Visual-Linguistic Representations for Multimodal Coreference Resolution
abstract: Represents dialogue, scene objects, and their relationships jointly for multimodal coreference resolution. Experiments require linking language mentions to visual objects across conversational context, offering transfer evidence for grounding message references to structured visual entities.

title: Performance Evaluation and Error Analysis for Multimodal Reference Resolution in a Conversation System
abstract: Evaluates multimodal reference resolution in a conversational system and analyzes errors arising from combining language with nonlinguistic input. It provides early empirical evidence on resolving references to visually or interactively available entities.

title: SpreadCluster: Recovering Versioned Spreadsheets through Similarity-Based Clustering
abstract: Learns similarity criteria such as worksheet-name and table-header features from known version groups and uses them to cluster spreadsheets likely to be versions of the same evolving artifact. It is evaluated on Enron spreadsheets and additional spreadsheet corpora and is used to construct the VEnron2 versioned corpus.
venue: 14th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR 2017)

title: Detecting and visualizing inter-worksheet smells in spreadsheets
abstract: Analyzes dependencies between worksheets and proposes inter-worksheet smells and visualizations for identifying problematic workbook structure. The approach is evaluated on spreadsheet corpora and industrial case studies, providing empirical evidence for workbook-level dependency analysis.

title: Tracing the lineage of view data in a warehousing environment
abstract: Defines and implements lineage tracing from derived warehouse view data back to the source data items that contributed to each result. The work handles query transformations including aggregation and provides transfer evidence for fine-grained derived-value-to-source provenance.

title: The T-Recs Table Recognition and Analysis System
abstract: Presents a bottom-up table structure recognizer that clusters word segments, constructs a tile structure, and recovers row- and column-spanning cells as well as sparse tables. It is designed to work across mixed-mode documents and low-quality OCR, making it foundational evidence for preserving nontrivial table topology.
venue: Document Analysis Systems: Theory and Practice

title: Navigating the Digital World as Humans Do: Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
abstract: Studies universal GUI grounding from natural-language references to elements in screenshots and builds large-scale training data from GUI elements and referring expressions. Evaluation across multiple GUI grounding benchmarks provides broad transfer evidence for language-to-region grounding on structured visual surfaces.

title: Doc-V*: Coarse-to-Fine Interactive Visual Reasoning for Multi-Page Document VQA
abstract: Presents coarse-to-fine reasoning over multi-page documents with iterative page retrieval, evidence accumulation, and structured working memory. The evaluation targets long multi-page document VQA and provides version-independent page-level evidence-selection results.

title: Detecting table clones and smells in spreadsheets
abstract: Introduces TableCheck for matching spreadsheet tables using header information and detecting inconsistent corresponding cells among table clones. The empirical evaluation studies spreadsheets in the EUSES corpus and provides evidence about correspondence among copied and independently evolving spreadsheet regions.
venue: 24th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2016)

title: Document Image Verification Based on Paragraph Alignment and Subtle Change Detection
abstract: Compares an input document image against a corresponding reference document by retrieving the reference, aligning paragraphs using structural features, and detecting subtle content changes under print-scan distortions. Experiments on constructed document-image databases evaluate both correspondence and change detection.

title: Class-Agnostic Region-of-Interest Matching in Document Images
abstract: Defines a document-image task in which a user-selected reference region must be matched to the corresponding region in another target document image. The proposed benchmark covers multiple difficulty levels and the baseline uses Siamese feature extraction and cross-attention to align semantically similar regions at multiple granularities.

title: Image-based table recognition: data, model, and evaluation
abstract: Introduces PubTabNet and an image-to-structured-table approach that reconstructs table contents and HTML structure from document images. It also introduces a structure-aware evaluation measure, providing stronger evidence for preserving cell organization than table detection alone.

title: Reading order detection on handwritten documents
abstract: Studies reading-order recovery in handwritten documents using document structure and contextual relationships. Although the domain is handwritten material rather than workplace email, the structural ordering problem is transferable to preserving document semantics.

title: TUTA: Tree-based Transformers for Generally Structured Table Pre-training
abstract: Represents generally structured tables with tree-based positional and structural information and pretrains a transformer over that hierarchy. It directly addresses hierarchical headers and semantic table structure rather than treating tables as flat sequences.

title: TURL: Table Understanding through Representation Learning
abstract: Learns contextual representations for relational tables and applies them to table-understanding tasks involving entities and semantic relationships. Because its input is already structured tables, it is transferable to downstream reasoning but does not solve extraction from document images.

title: Visual Understanding of Complex Table Structures from Document Images
abstract: Targets visually complex tables whose semantics depend on nontrivial row, column, and spanning-cell organization. It is relevant to preserving structural relations that are easily lost when tables are flattened into plain text.

title: TaPas: Weakly Supervised Table Parsing via Pre-training
abstract: Pretrains a model for answering questions over tables using cell selection and aggregation. It demonstrates cell-level reasoning over already normalized tables, so it is transferable to downstream evidence selection rather than direct document-table extraction.

title: M3Grounder: Mask-Based Multi-Span and Multi-Granular Grounding for Document QA
abstract: Grounds document-QA evidence using masks and supports multiple evidence spans at different granularities such as phrases, lines, and blocks. This directly addresses precise localization of source evidence rather than only producing an answer or relevant page.

title: Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Studies referring-expression grounding in images where scene text is important for identifying the referenced region. The task is transferable to screenshots and document surfaces because successful grounding depends on jointly interpreting text and visual location.

title: RefChartQA: Grounding Visual Answer on Chart Images through Instruction Tuning
abstract: Extends chart question answering toward explicit visual grounding of answers in chart images. This makes it directly relevant to requirements where answers must be tied back to the chart elements or regions that support them.

title: Hierarchical multimodal transformers for Multi-Page DocVQA
abstract: Introduces a hierarchical architecture for question answering over multi-page documents and the MP-DocVQA setting. It jointly handles page selection and answer generation, providing page-level provenance but not necessarily cell- or bounding-box-level evidence.

title: MMLongBench-Doc: Benchmarking Long-context Document Understanding with Visualizations
abstract: Benchmarks long-document multimodal understanding over PDFs containing text, images, charts, tables, and layout information. Questions may require locating evidence across pages, making the benchmark useful for studying cross-page reasoning and source attribution.

title: LongDocURL: a Comprehensive Multimodal Long Document Benchmark Integrating Understanding, Reasoning, and Locating
abstract: Evaluates long multimodal documents with tasks spanning understanding, reasoning, and locating. Its explicit locating component is especially relevant to systems that must return not only an answer but also where supporting evidence occurs.

title: DocFormer: End-to-End Transformer for Document Understanding
abstract: Presents an end-to-end multimodal transformer that combines text, visual appearance, and spatial information for document understanding. It is relevant to preserving page structure and associations between OCR content and visual regions.

title: InfographicVQA
abstract: Introduces question answering over infographics where information is distributed among text, graphics, and spatial layout. The benchmark is directly relevant to multimodal page understanding and transferable to image-rich workplace attachments.

title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
abstract: Studies document evidence attribution without requiring models to directly emit coordinates. Models quote supporting text and a multimodal retriever maps those quotations back to page regions, providing an alternative route from answer evidence to precise source location.

title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
abstract: Presents a version-aware RAG framework that models document evolution with a hierarchical graph containing version sequences, content boundaries, and changes between document states. Retrieval routes version-sensitive questions through version filtering and change-tracking paths.

title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning
abstract: Models long-document VQA as evidence-graph reasoning. The framework performs evidence localization, structured document parsing, and explicit graph construction with node-level provenance so evidence composition across multiple pages can be inspected.

title: Disambiguating Reference in Visually Grounded Dialogues through Joint Modeling of Textual and Multimodal Semantic Structures
abstract: Unifies textual reference resolution and grounding to visual objects in dialogue, with particular attention to ambiguous pronouns and ellipses. This is transfer evidence for references in communication text that point into an associated visual artifact.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Multimomal Generation for Document Question Answering
abstract: Introduces MMDocRAG for long multimodal documents containing text, images, and tables. Its questions include multi-page cross-modal evidence chains and its evaluation explicitly measures multimodal evidence selection and integration.

title: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
abstract: Evaluates agents on professional spreadsheet generation, debugging, and visualization workflows involving complex workbooks. Tasks average many worksheets and require coordinated modifications and cross-sheet dependencies rather than isolated table operations.

title: Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Defines a referring-expression task in which linguistic descriptions can refer to text visible inside an image. Its model explicitly aligns scene-text semantics, visual regions, and referring expressions, making it a close transfer analogue for references such as labels or highlighted content in screenshots.

title: Heterogeneous Element-Aware Cross-Version Differencing of Scientific Documents via Layout-Aware Alignment and Structure-Aware Reasoning
abstract: Proposes a layout-aware cross-version differencing framework that decomposes scientific PDFs into typed text, table, formula, and figure elements, aligns corresponding elements using spatial, content, and structural compatibility, and localizes semantic changes between document revisions.

title: SentryLine: Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Evolving Documents in Oncology Care
abstract: Describes evidence-grounded QA over living oncology guidelines. The system returns inline citations, temporal verification, and drift information when guideline documents have changed across versions.

title: Towards Robust Real-World Spreadsheet Understanding with Multi-Agent Multi-Format Reasoning
abstract: Presents SpreadsheetAgent, which incrementally inspects spreadsheet regions through code results, rendered images, and LaTeX tables. It first constructs structural sketches and row or column summaries and then verifies relevant regions during downstream reasoning.

title: Where is this coming from? Making groundedness count in the evaluation of Document VQA models
abstract: Proposes Document VQA evaluation metrics that account for both semantic correctness and multimodal placement of an answer in its source document. Human evaluation is used to validate whether the grounded scoring better distinguishes supported from poorly grounded predictions.

title: TRH2TQA: Table Recognition with Hierarchical Relationships to Table Question-Answering on Business Table Images
abstract: Extracts business-table images into structured representations that preserve merged cells and parent-child header relationships before performing table QA. The work directly targets hierarchical table structure needed to interpret complex financial documents.

title: Look as You Think: Unifying Reasoning and Visual Evidence Attribution for Verifiable Document RAG via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Introduces a Chain-of-Evidence representation that attaches reasoning references to document regions using bounding boxes and page indexes. The reinforcement-learning method trains models to generate answers together with progressively attributable visual evidence.

title: DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding
abstract: Represents enterprise-document text together with bounding-box layout information and models cross-alignment between semantic and spatial modalities. It targets irregular layouts and heterogeneous business documents such as forms, invoices, reports, and contracts.

title: MAGE-RAG: Multigranular Adaptive Graph Evidence for Agentic Multimodal RAG in Long-Document QA
abstract: Models long documents as an evidence graph containing page- and element-level nodes with relationships such as containment, reading order, layout adjacency, and section hierarchy. Unlike page-only retrieval, it exposes finer-grained document elements for evidence selection, though it does not address cross-version lineage.

title: CiteVQA: Benchmarking Evidence Attribution for Trustworthy Document Intelligence
abstract: Benchmarks document question answering in which a system must provide an answer together with element-level bounding-box citations to the supporting source regions. It directly evaluates answer attribution inside document pages, but does not add cross-version attachment lineage.

title: From Rows to Reasoning: A Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Framework for Spreadsheet Understanding
abstract: Targets enterprise spreadsheets with multiple linked sheets and multimodal content such as embedded images. It builds retrieval units at multiple spreadsheet granularities, providing direct evidence for workbook-level multimodal understanding but not comprehensive revision provenance.

title: HierDoc: Hierarchical Page-to-Region Evidence Routing for Long-Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Uses hierarchical evidence routing that first identifies relevant pages and then selects supporting semantic regions within those pages. Region representations can include crops, OCR text, and table content, making the work directly relevant to hierarchical document evidence localization.

title: Change-Centric Management of Versions in an XML Warehouse
abstract: A structured-document precursor for cross-version lineage. The work stores evolving XML snapshots through completed deltas and persistent identifiers, allowing changes between successive versions to be represented without treating each document snapshot as unrelated.

title: Bridging the gap between tracking and detecting changes in XML
abstract: Connects explicit change tracking with post-hoc differencing so that higher-level document changes can be represented rather than only low-level text edits. This is relevant to revision semantics and element lineage, though it operates on XML rather than rendered multimodal documents.

title: Schema-less, semantics-based change detection for XML documents
abstract: Associates XML elements across successive versions without requiring a schema and uses semantics to preserve identifiers through substantial structural change. It is particularly relevant to stable element identity when revisions alter document organization.

title: Rethinking Reading Order: Toward Generalizable Document Understanding with LLM-based Relation Modeling
abstract: Uses language-model-based relation modeling to infer global reading order and inter-element layout relationships. The work is relevant to hierarchical document structure because it models dependencies between elements rather than treating OCR blocks independently.

title: Robust Table Detection and Structure Recognition from Heterogeneous Document Images
abstract: Performs table detection and structural reconstruction on heterogeneous document images, including difficult structures involving spanning cells and blank areas. The explicit recovery of cell topology is relevant to preserving source-cell semantics before downstream grounding.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Introduces distinct notions of why-provenance and where-provenance for database query results, formalizing both justification and source location. This is transfer evidence for exact source attribution, not direct evidence for multimodal documents or revised attachments.
